@graph.headline: What a Custom Home Builder Website Must Include
@graph.description: See the pages, proof, process, people, qualification, and next step a custom home builder website must include so the right buyers can trust the work.

mainEntity.name: What must a custom home builder website include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom home builder website must include a first screen that names fit and geography, project stories with decision context, a realistic process, current people and roles, respectful qualification, attributable trust signals, research-phase answers, a next step that explains what happens, and a mobile experience that is usable.

mainEntity.name: What belongs on the first screen of a builder website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Within a few seconds the visitor should see what kind of builder you are, who you serve, where you work, the project or relationship you are best suited for, and the next reasonable step. Keep competing buttons, autoplay video, and vague award claims off that first screen.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a website lead and a qualified custom-home inquiry?

acceptedAnswer.text: A website lead is any form fill, phone call, chat start, or booked click. A qualified custom-home inquiry is a person whose geography, project type, planning horizon, decision role, and investment conversation are a plausible fit for the work the builder actually does.

mainEntity.name: Should a builder website publish investment ranges online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if the range can stay current and honest. Add geography, assumptions, date, inclusions, and a review cadence. If a number would mislead, explain the variables and the point at which a responsible conversation can happen.

mainEntity.name: What trust signals need context on a builder website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reviews, awards, credentials, partnerships, and press need a source, a named organization, a date when relevance can change, and permission for customer language. A logo strip without that context does not prove the promise.

mainEntity.name: How should a builder website measure success?

acceptedAnswer.text: Track which pages qualified visitors use, which questions introduce the brand, which CTAs start a meaningful action, whether submissions fit the market and timing, and which leads sales accepts. Conversion reporting is pending validation until analytics, forms, calls, bookings, and CRM use the same definitions.
